title: Overnight incident afterlist - followups and runbook TODOs
body:
Brief: Pager at 02:14 UTC for elevated error-rate on hosted-api->generation-route. Signal: 5xx spike + backend timeouts from serving-runtime. Alert source: prometheus rule 'redwood_api_5xx_rate_high'.

Timeline (my notes):
- 02:14 — Pager -> glance at Grafana (error-rate ~9.6% over 5m, baseline <0.5%).
- 02:16 — Quick triage with Marco via PM; confirmed spikes concentrated to 4 regions (us-west1 eu-west1 ap-south1 us-east1).
- 02:20 — Throttled retries offload, switched routing policy to fallback-model for a small % (20%) to reduce pressure.
- 02:29 — Error-rate started decreasing to ~3.2%.
- 03:05 — Stabilized around 0.4% after autoscale bump + routing change.
- 04:10 — Post-incident, started followups and runbook notes.

Immediate mitigation steps executed:
- Increased pool size for dedicated-inference-pool-7 by +2 nodes (manual override) — helped queue drain.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefix-caching for a subset of traffic (rollout id roll/2027-03-20/2) to avoid cache thrashing.
- Applied routing fallback to model-variant-b (lower mem footprint) for non-premium tier.
- Bumped request timeout from 45s -> 60s for long-tail jobs (temporary).

Initial hypothesis (why):
- Root cause likely a combination of: recent kernel upgrade on a subset of GPU hosts (change window 2027-03-19 23:30 UTC) + increased sequence length percentiles from a customer rollout (spike of long-context requests).
- Observed OOM/kernel-restart events in host logs (~02:10-02:18) for 3 machines in pool-7.
- KV-cache invalidation patterns show bursty churn around same time (concurrent writes from caching service).

Evidence collected (links/log ids):
- Host logs: host-7a3f - dmesg & journalctl snippets -> KERNEL:oom_kill messages. (see attached logs in SRE-INC-2027-0423)
- Serving runtime trace: trace-id 7f2b-0319-rtc (shows requeue attempts and 504s).
- Grafana dashboard snapshots: /dashboards/redwood/api/5xx-spike/2027-03-20-02

Runbook / playbook gaps discovered:
- No explicit pre-step for detecting kernel module mismatch on host-side post-kernel-upgrade (we assume infra will block dangerous kernels).
- Cache invalidation poorly instrumented — need a visible metric showing invalidation rate per pool.
- No automatic rollback trigger for recent config that touches prefix-caching; only manual.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- (Lynn) Draft runbook addendum: "Kernel-upgrade detection and rollback checklist". Include commands to query host kernel versions, automated filter against allowed list. ETA: 2027-03-24.
- (Marco) Add metric 'kv_cache_invalidation_rate{pool}' to prometheus, and dashboard panel. ETA: 2027-03-26.
- (Aisha) Create alert rule: 'kv_cache_invalidation_burst' -> paged if > X/sec for >1m. ETA: 2027-03-22.
- (Infra team contact: Dana) Investigate why kernel upgrade rolled into production pool-7 despite gating. Raise postmortem for infra release process. Requested by: 2027-03-23.
- (SRE) Create an automated canary for prefix-caching changes that will run synthetic long-context requests to detect thrash. Owner tbd. ETA: 2027-04-01.

Runbook TODO checklist (quick actionable):
- [ ] Add explicit kernel-version allowlist check to node-provisioning playbook. (Lynn)
- [ ] Document safe strategy for cache invalidation (staggered/rolling). (Marco)
- [ ] Add rollback step in prefix-caching rollout (automated flag). (Product/Runtime)
- [ ] Add a post-incident note template for infra change windows to include host kernel versions. (Lynn)

Notes to self / quick commands I used:
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | grep pool-7
- ssh host-7a3f 'journalctl -u serving-runtime --since "2027-03-20 01:45"' > host-7a3f-journal.log
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'pool-7'" --format="table(name,status,zone,machineType)"

Open questions / unresolved:
- Was there a coordinated infra deploy (kernel) across multiple regions? Infra runbook says staged, but logs show same kernel arrival window. Need infra confirmation.
- What customer rollout produced the long-context spike? Product/solutions might have a rollout id.
- Should we set a hard cap on sequence length for non-premium traffic at the gateway to protect capacity?

Post-incident comms plan:
- Short blurb to incident channel summarizing mitigations + owner assignments (send by 2027-03-21 10:00 local).
- If infra confirms kernel issue, escalate to ops-retro and include recommended gating changes.

Later follow-up references:
- SRE-INC-2027-0423 (incident ticket)
- Confluence draft: kv-cache-fallback (link above)

If I forget tomorrow: check with Dana about kernel gating, ping Marco for dashboard PR, and set a calendar reminder to review the canary plan on 2027-03-30.

End notes: felt messy overnight but mitigations worked; major win: routing fallback saved headroom so premium traffic remained stable. Keep runbook changes minimal and testable.

-- Lynn
